goals: Mechanistic: quantify how soil clay content controls the partitioning of infiltrated water between surface runoff and sub-surface drainage/recharge, under fixed forcing and vegetation
Validation (optional): check the response against physical expectation and published clay-partitioning relationships (no co-located obs required)
key_processes: unsaturated-zone hydraulic conductivity and matric potential as functions of texture

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM directly simulates the vertical water balance and outputs runoff (QOVER) and drainage/recharge (QDRAI); a single-factor clay sweep under fixed forcing isolates the texture control cleanly.

answerable: Effect of clay content on surface runoff fraction (QOVER)
Effect of clay content on sub-surface drainage / recharge (QDRAI), PROVIDED spin-up or WTD-informed warm start is included
Shape/curvature of the partitioning response across 5-55% clay

sampling_strategy.n_justification: One column per clay level. Six evenly spaced levels spanning the requested 5-55% range resolve the expected nonlinear (strongest at high clay) shift in partitioning without redundant runs; endpoints anchor the range and four interior points capture curvature.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Controlled / not spatial — all treatments share one representative forcing location and period; only clay fraction differs.
sampling_strategy.replication: None — deterministic model, controlled experiment; no stochastic replication needed. Everything except clay is held fixed.

sampling_plan.reason: Low-clay baseline: high conductivity, recharge/drainage-dominated partitioning expected
Interior level to trace the recharge-dominated portion of the response curve
Mid-range loam-like level, transition region of the partitioning response
Interior level where reduced conductivity begins shifting water toward runoff
High-clay level capturing accelerating runoff fraction (curvature)
Upper end-member: low conductivity, runoff-dominated partitioning expected

validation_design.comparison: analog — qualitative/quantitative check that the modelled response is monotonic in the expected direction and of plausible magnitude; NOT co-located observation validation (none exist and none are required for a conceptual experiment)
validation_design.metric: sign and monotonicity of dQOVER/dclay, partitioning ratio vs clay curve shape

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: one representative fixed forcing period + fixed vegetation/slope; synthetic soil varying ONLY clay fraction; spin-up / WTD-informed warm start applied identically to all columns

requires_capabilities.capability: synthetic soil parameterization that sweeps clay fraction while holding all other soil inputs fixed (or deriving them deterministically from clay via one documented pedotransfer function)
requires_capabilities.why: The controlled experiment requires varying ONLY clay; the configurator must expose clay as an isolated lever rather than pulling a full SSURGO texture bundle
requires_capabilities.blocks: Clean isolation of the clay effect — without it, other covarying soil properties confound the result

requires_capabilities.capability: model spin-up years OR WTD-informed warm start applied identically across all clay levels
requires_capabilities.why: Recharge/drainage are slow states; cold-start columns read ~0 recharge while storage fills from the default ~8.8 m water table, so unspun recharge differences would be initialization artifacts, not clay responses
requires_capabilities.blocks: The recharge half of the partitioning question

requires_capabilities.capability: single fixed representative forcing (one location + period, applied to all treatments)
requires_capabilities.why: "Holding everything else fixed" demands identical climate forcing across all clay levels so the response is attributable to clay alone

assumptions: Clay range 5-55% refers to mass clay fraction in the mineral soil; other texture components adjust deterministically or non-clay properties are held at fixed reference values.
A single representative forcing location/period within CONUS 1980-2018 is acceptable as the fixed climate; choice affects magnitudes but not the qualitative clay response.
Vegetation type, slope, and soil depth/layering are held at fixed reference values across all treatments.
Recharge is proxied by ELM sub-surface drainage/aquifer recharge (QDRAI); runoff by QOVER.
No observational validation is required for this conceptual experiment; benchmark is physical expectation.
open_questions: Should non-clay soil properties be held at fixed reference values, or derived from clay via a pedotransfer function? (Both are defensible; they answer slightly different questions.)
Which single forcing location/period should be the fixed climate? (A humid vs semi-arid choice will shift the runoff/recharge baseline.)
How many spin-up years (or warm-start) are acceptable given cost, to ensure recharge has equilibrated for every clay level?
Is a finer clay resolution near the high-clay end desired if the response proves strongly nonlinear there?
